ch02.caption: Pan Hannian, born 1906, a native of Yixing, Jiangsu. He joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1925, moved to the hidden front in April 1931 as chief of the Central Special Branch's Second Section, and from the latter half of 1932 directed the work of the Central Special Branch.

ch02.caption: Zhao Rong, that is, Kang Sheng, born 1898, a native of Zhucheng, Shandong. He joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1925, and after 1931 served as head of the CCP Central Organization Department, a member of the provisional Political Bureau, and chief of the Central Special Branch's Third Section; from early 1932 he directed the work of the Central Special Branch.

ch02.caption: Chen Lifu, born 1900, a native of Huzhou, Zhejiang. In February 1928 the Kuomintang Central Standing Committee named Chiang Kai-shek concurrent head of the Organization Department; on Chen Guofu's advice Chiang set up a separate Investigation Section to monitor, investigate, and strike at rival parties, and Chen Lifu thereby became its first chief.

ch02.caption: When Bao Junfu served as the Investigation Section's Shanghai special commissioner, he set up his office in an over-the-street building like this one, said to have stood opposite Dade Lane on North Sichuan Road (today's Sichuan North Road) in Shanghai.
